messages.subject: How should I model s-curves with lavaan?
parts:
I have simulated a set of s-curves using the logistic function. When I attempt to fit a growth curve model, I get: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative.

My model looks like the following.

i =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3 + 1*y4 + 1*y5 + 1*y6 + 1*y7 + 1*y8 + 1*y9 + 1*y10 + 1*y11 + 1*y12 + 1*y13 + 1*y14 + 1*y15 + 1*y16 + 1*y17
s =~ 0*y1 + 1*y2 + 2*y3 + 3*y4 + 4*y5 + 5*y6 + 6*y7 + 7*y8 + 8*y9 + 9*y10 + 10*y11 + 11*y12 + 12*y13 + 13*y14 + 14*y15 + 15*y16 + 16*y17

A summary(fit) shows the following. I am wondering if the problem is with the simulation or with the modeling? Or is there no problem? I wonder if there is something else I am missing. Even if I do a log transform against the y1,...,y17 values, I get the nearly the same outputs. Any help is appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: How should I model s-curves with lavaan?
parts:
Two things. Try re-scaling the slope loadings by a factor of 10 (0,
.1, .2, etc.) to reduce round-off problems.

Second, you generated logistic data and fit a linear model. Misfit is
likely the primary problem.

parts:
Patrick,

1. With regards to "misfit", are you saying that this approach might not be appropriate? I read this article http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.510.3049&rep=rep1&type=pdf where non-linear growth curves are log-transformed and then fitted. The Demo.growth data does not seem to be linear either (by linear, i mean a straight line for t1, t2, t3, t4). 

2. On the other hand, I have raw data (e.g. 1, 3, 4) that I turn into a cumulative distribution curve (e.g. 0.13, 0.50, 1.0). The cumulative percent curve is modeled as a s-curve and can be fitted with a parameterized logistic function. I "think" your suggestion might be to use the raw data instead?

.1, .2, etc.) to reduce round-off problems.

likely the primary problem.

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: How should I model s-curves with lavaan?
parts:
I think what you are looking for is the prediction with the logistic function, when X predict Y follows

Y = (a) / (1 + exp(b-cX) )

Where A is your upper asymptote, C your lower asymptote, and b your regression slope.

I am not sure how to do this with lavaan. I could think of doing this with nlme or brms

On Monday, July 13, 2020 at 6:36:56 PM UTC-5 mal...@malonequantitative.com wrote:
I haven't read that article, but you said you generated sigmoid data
and then your model forces a straight line. The model is mis-specified
with respect to the data-generating mechanism. Anything can happen.

messages.subject: Re: How should I model s-curves with lavaan?
parts:
It can be done with lavaan with "phantom variables."

Grimm & Ram have syntax for doing it in Mplus in Appendix A here:
https://www.statmodel.com/download/SEM-Grimm2009.pdf (though of course
you should read the whole article for context). They don't use
anything lavaan can't do.

Pat
